about.title: Mammoth Lakes Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Mammoth Lakes' economy runs on seasonal tourism, hospitality, and outdoor recreation work — jobs that come with real physical risk, from lift operations to kitchen shifts to snow removal along Minaret Road and Rt 203. When a workplace injury happens, California law generally routes the claim through workers' compensation rather than a lawsuit against your employer. But that's not always the end of the story: if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. Mono County's smaller size means fewer local resources for navigating these overlapping systems, which is exactly why getting matched with an attorney familiar with both tracks matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything — we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can review the details of your specific situation and explain your options clearly, without pressure or guesswork about outcomes.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Mammoth Lakes Work Injury

items.title: Understanding the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp eligibility. An attorney can help make sure this deadline and related paperwork don't slip through the cracks.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, a claim against a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — often requires separate legal action. An independent attorney can evaluate whether your injury involves someone outside your employer.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file workers' comp claims. If you're worried about your job status after an injury, an attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt working at a Mammoth Lakes resort — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. However, if a third party — such as equipment manufacturer or a subcontractor — contributed to the accident, a separate injury claim may be possible alongside workers' comp. An independent attorney can review the facts and explain which paths apply to you.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. Waiting longer can complicate your claim, so it's best to report promptly even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury in Mammoth Lakes?
items.answer: No — California law makes it illegal for employers to retaliate against workers for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options for addressing it.
